readme.summary: The README contains only badges and links with no actual documentation content, forcing users to visit external documentation.
readme.top_issue: Zero inline documentation - no description of what the tool does, no installation steps, no usage examples, everything deferred to external docs link

injection_risks.description: The includeUnmarshaler function uses os.ReadFile to read files specified by the !include tag, which could lead to arbitrary file reads if an attacker can manipulate the YAML input.
The includeUnmarshaler function uses readDir to read directories specified by the !include_dir tag, which could lead to arbitrary directory reads if an attacker can manipulate the YAML input.
The Init function uses fmt.Sprintf to construct a PowerShell command string, which could lead to command injection if an attacker can manipulate the shellName or configPath inputs.

critical_findings: Arbitrary file reads via the !include tag in YAML input.
Command injection via the Init function's PowerShell command string construction.
security.summary: The aliae package has several security concerns, including arbitrary file reads and command injection vulnerabilities, but does not appear to expose sensitive secrets or have overly permissive default configurations.

common_complaints: Missing features for shell integration (Nushell autoload)
Lack of environment variable access in templates
praise_themes: Users comparing positively to Oh My Posh (suggesting good design patterns)
